focus.jnote: The scan boarded two grain-ETF breakouts into a weekend that reignited the Iran war — that’s the story. U.S. Central Command struck Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz, and Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said Sunday they targeted U.S. military bases in Jordan and the UAE in retaliation for the first American strikes on Iran in weeks, after CENTCOM announced strikes against Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz. Oil surged — crude jumped after fresh fighting flared in the Strait of Hormuz, with Brent for November rising above $90 a barrel while West Texas Intermediate was near $86. On the Fed: Warsh said in Jackson Hole Friday that inflation was running too hot and the central bank has ‘work to do,’ and over the weekend traders lifted their bets for a 25 bp hike at the next meeting to 62%, up from roughly 40% a week ago. Equity futures reflect the risk-off shift — Dow futures fell 0.1%, S&P 500 futures declined 0.2% and Nasdaq-100 contracts dropped 0.1%, though all three indexes were on track to post monthly gains. The overriding gate: an active, open-ended oil shock stacked on a hawkish Fed is exactly the tape a Sniper does not sell premium into.

focus.notup: No bearish single-name boarded today. The natural bearish leans in this tape — airlines and other fuel-sensitive cyclicals pressured by the oil spike, or rate-sensitive long-duration tech into a hawkish Warsh — are two-sided war/rate trades, not clean Snipers. A ceasefire or de-escalation headline squeezes any short violently, and selling bear calls into a VIX that is starting to rise carries its own blow-up risk. The disciplined answer is to sell nothing new today.

First, the environment: an active U.S.–Iran military exchange in the Strait of Hormuz with oil above $90 is an unscheduled, open-ended tail — you cannot time or size around the next headline. Second, a hawkish Warsh has lifted September rate-hike odds to ~62%, an added macro overhang. P(≥1% gap) at 44% sits well above the 35% trigger, and composite 66 is deep in WARM. risks: Iran retaliation & escalation — Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said Sunday they targeted U.S. military bases in Jordan and the UAE in retaliation for the U.S. strikes on Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz; any further strike on personnel or bases gaps the whole tape instantly. This is the number-one thing to watch.

Strait of Hormuz shipping — Kharg Island, which handles roughly 90% of Iran’s oil exports, was reportedly targeted, and the strait once carried a fifth of the world’s energy exports. Any attack on that infrastructure or a full closure sends crude vertical — the week’s biggest tail.

Hawkish Warsh & the September FOMC — Warsh said Friday inflation was running too hot and the Fed has ‘work to do,’ and weekend traders lifted 25 bp Sept-hike odds to 62%, up from ~40% a week ago. A hawkish repricing on top of an oil shock is the worst macro combination.

August jobs report · Fri — with earnings season largely over and a quiet Monday data calendar, investors will turn toward the Labor Department’s monthly jobs report on Friday. A hot or cold print reprices hike odds again — keep spreads clear of the release.

Oil → inflation → yields — oil prices jumped on worries the conflict could escalate, with Brent above $88, and the ongoing Iran war has been a key factor keeping inflation concerns alive. A sustained oil bid feeds the rate-fear narrative and pressures long-duration stocks.
